title: POC SDK + Toolflow and Structured Output — Weekly Pulse
summary: Weekly check-in on POC integration: SDK usage, function/tool calling stability, structured output schema drift and first round of tuning. Covered observed regressions on long prefixes, retry/fallback behavior, and next steps for sandbox benchmarks and security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to share small benchmark script + sandbox creds
Customer to run 3 workload samples and report token distribution
Schedule deep-dive on dedicated capacity if latency targets not met
action_items: Maya Patel - send sandbox creds + sample benchmark script - due 2026-01-25
Ethan Rivera - prepare short repro for prefix KV cache regression and share kernel traces - due 2026-01-27
Priya Singh - run 3 representative workloads and upload token histograms - due 2026-01-28
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 min | Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Zoë (Redwood) — Jonah, Priya, Sam, Nina (Aurelia)

Summary (auto): weekly POC pulse; focus on SDK tool-calls and structured output stability.

[00:00] Maya: alright team, thanks for joining — I think we have, um, about 40 minutes. quick check in on the pilot integration. how's everyone doing?
[00:18] Jonah: doing good, thanks. been a busy week, we ran the first three scenario tests against the sandbox. saw some oddities with multi-step calls.
[00:30] Priya: yea, the function calling path sometimes returns partial JSON and then a free text follow-on that breaks our parser. may be due to truncation or the model switching to stream mode mid-response.
[00:45] Ethan: ok that's helpful — can you paste an example in the shared doc? is it consistently at longer prefixes or at specific templates?
[01:00] Priya: mostly longer prefixes where we prime with patient history; token counts spike. also noticed KV cache re-use seems to be inconsistent — sometimes it hits, sometimes not. transcription note: they said K V cash earlier.
[01:20] Zoë: for the KV behaviour, we instrumented the SDK to surface cache hit-metrics. do you have that on your side?
[01:30] Sam: we have logs but it's noisy. we didn't correlate with token windows yet.
[01:40] Maya: quick qualification — what's your latency SLO for the call chain and what's acceptable cost per 1k tokens in this POC?
[01:52] Jonah: target p99 under 600ms for single-turn calls, for multi-step chains we're okay up to 1.2s, but cost ideally under $0.30 per 1k tokens equivalent.
[02:05] Ethan: got it. that's helpful. two levers we typically adjust: batching and quantization profile for the selected model. also fallback routing to smaller variants if dedicated capacity is constrained.
[02:20] Nina: on security — we need to confirm KMS integration for private deployment and what audit logs look like in Redwood Private.
[02:35] Maya: we'll share the security pack, includes KMS/HSM notes and sample audit events; I'll add that to the drive link.
[02:48] Priya: there's also an intermittent 502 coming from the SDK when tool-calls trigger external webhooks — we suspect a retry/backoff mismatch.
[03:00] Ethan: can you show a replay of one of those traces? backoff config defaults in the SDK are 3 retries with exponential backoff; if your webhook takes >5s it can cascade.
[03:15] Priya: i'll attach traces.
[03:22] Sam: also curious about streaming vs non-streaming — for our UI we prefer streaming partial function outputs so the user sees progress, but streaming complicates structured output enforcement.
[03:36] Zoë: yeah streaming and strict JSON schema are in tension. we recommend function-calling with final structured output when determinism matters, and streaming for UX with a validation pass that normalizes.
[03:52] Jonah: is there an SDK helper to do that validation? we don't want to re-implement heavy parsing on our side.
[03:59] Maya: Ethan, quick pointer?
[04:03] Ethan: there is a small helper in the JS/py SDK to validate and rehydrate function responses against a JSON schema; we'll push a PR to the sandbox repo. it's experimental but should speed you up.
[04:18] Priya: perfect. that might also catch the partial JSON cases.
[04:25] Maya: ok let's walk through the three main pain points you called out: 1) partial/streaming JSON, 2) KV cache misses, 3) webhook retry 502s.
[04:38] Priya: yes.
[04:40] Maya: for (1) we'll share the SDK validation helper and recommend switching to final function call for critical outputs; for (2) Ethan will investigate kernel/exec path to see why cache isn't consistent under long prefixes; for (3) recommend increasing webhook timeout and adjusting SDK retry/backoff settings — we can also route tool calls through Redwood-managed proxy in sandbox for debugging.
[05:05] Jonah: sounds good. what about dedicated vs hosted? if we can't hit p99 latency, we may consider Redwood Dedicated, but we need pricing and lead times.
[05:18] Maya: Dedicated lead time is typically 2–4 weeks after contract, pricing varies by commit; i'll include a rough TCO calc in the follow-up along with performance delta numbers from our catalog.
[05:33] Sam: please include quantized model options — our infra team prefers smaller models if quality holds.
[05:40] Ethan: we'll add quantization profiles and recommended batch sizes per scenario. note: batching trades throughput for latency — we'll suggest micro-batching settings.
[05:55] Priya: one more item — we run data residency checks. are there region options for private (EU)?
[06:05] Maya: Redwood Private supports EU regions; in the private control plane you can pin region and we support KMS key residency; i'll add the region matrix to the security pack.
[06:18] Nina: great. also, what's the retention window for audit logs in sandbox vs Private?
[06:26] Maya: sandbox default is 30 days; Private is configurable up to 365 with add-on.
[06:33] Jonah: ok thanks.
[06:36] [10 min mark — deeper notes and tradeoffs omitted for brevity]
[10:05] Ethan: i dug into the kernel traces from a similar customer: the mis-hit pattern happens when the prompt has long overlapping context windows that force the runtime to fall back to a slower KV eviction path. i'll prepare a repro with kernel timings.
[10:25] Priya: if you can reproduce in sandbox we'll tweak our prompts, that might be faster than infra changes.
[10:34] Zoë: small note on SDK usage: avoid re-instantiating the client per turn, keep a long-lived client to preserve connection reuse and KV locality. some of the 502s come from connection churn.
[10:50] Sam: good call, we had a bug in our loop that re-created the client per user message.
[11:00] Maya: ok another area: function calling reliability when multiple tools are chained — if tool A fails we surface a deterministic fallback. what's your desired behavior?
[11:12] Jonah: ideally try once, then fallback to cached answer; if cached not present, escalate to human. we want idempotent behavior.
[11:20] Ethan: SDK supports middleware to implement that; we'll share sample middleware for idempotent retries.
[11:30] Priya: on structured outputs, we noticed model sometimes uses synonyms for fields (e.g., patient_id -> pid). can the validation layer map aliases?
[11:45] Zoë: yes the schema helper supports alias mapping and a small canonicalization layer — we'll include a config example.
[11:55] Sam: any blockers on your side for next week?
[12:00] Priya: main blocker is reproducing the KV miss and partial JSON in sandbox. once we can repro we'll iterate.
[12:08] Ethan: i'll prioritize the repro and aim to have kernel traces and a patchable repro by Tue.
[12:15] Maya: i'll send the sandbox creds and sample benchmark script by EOD tomorrow plus the security pack and region matrix.
[12:25] Jonah: thanks, that helps. also can you include the expected token accounting so we can map cost estimates to our budget?
[12:34] Maya: yes, sample TCO + token accounting in the follow-up.
[12:40] Priya: one question — do we have recommended JSON schema size limits before the validator becomes expensive?
[12:48] Ethan: aim for under 20 fields and avoid nested arrays >100 items; if you need larger payloads use a secondary storage reference pattern.
[12:58] Zoë: also note that streaming large payloads increases chance of partial emission; prefer final function call for payloads >2k tokens.
[13:10] Sam: noted.
[13:15] Maya: ok let's do a quick recap and explicit next steps.
[13:20] Maya (recap): Redwood will: 1) share sandbox creds and benchmark script (Maya) 2) push SDK validation helper PR and middleware examples (Ethan/Zoë) 3) investigate KV cache repro and provide kernel traces (Ethan). Customer will: 4) run three workload samples and upload token histograms (Priya) 5) attach webhook traces for 502 (Priya/Sam). Security: 6) Redwood to share security pack and region matrix (Maya).
[13:55] Jonah: good, timeline sounds fine. we aim to have results before next week's sync.
[14:05] Maya: ok then i'll schedule the follow-up and include a 60-minute slot for a deep-dive if needed.
[14:12] Priya: thanks everyone.
[14:16] Meeting end.
